title: Georgian Language Benchmark: Two Biggest AI Labs Clash in a Language That Doesn't Play by Anyone's Rules
why_read: A hands-on benchmark comparing how major LLMs handle Georgian, a low-resource morphologically complex language, with concrete findings on generation versus comprehension gaps.
analysis: This is an independent benchmarking effort testing leading AI models' ability to understand and produce Georgian, a language with unusual grammar and script that stresses tokenization and generation differently than most benchmarks. The author reports that comprehension is largely solved while production remains weak, numbers are especially error-prone, and token costs are higher for some models in this language. This kind of low-resource-language evaluation is valuable because most LLM benchmarks are English-centric and this fills a real gap, though it's an informal single-author project rather than peer-reviewed work. Readers interested in multilingual NLP or practical LLM limitations would find concrete, specific findings here.
